source_title: J. C. Penney Company, Inc. - Form 10-K (Fiscal Year ended February 2, 2013)
publisher_issuer: J. C. Penney Company, Inc. (filed with U.S. SEC, EDGAR CIK 0001166126); corroborated by TIME and Retail Dive
company_context: J. C. Penney is a mid-tier U.S. department-store chain. In November 2011 it hired former Apple retail chief Ron Johnson as CEO. On January 25, 2012 Johnson announced a sweeping pricing overhaul, 'Fair and Square' everyday-low-pricing, eliminating the hundreds of coupons and promotional sales the chain's core customers were conditioned to. The change took effect February 1, 2012.
business_type: Department-store / mid-tier apparel and home retail (bricks-and-mortar)
macro_context: Post-recession recovery; promotion-driven department-store sector under pressure from off-price (TJX, Ross) and fast fashion; consumers strongly habituated to coupons and sale events.
evidence_summary: Johnson removed couponing and high-low promotional pricing in favor of 'Fair and Square' everyday prices. Core customers, who derived value perception from discounts, sharply reduced spending. Comparable-store sales fell every quarter through 2012 (Q1 -18.9%, Q2 -21.7%, Q3 -26.1%, Q4 -4.4% per quarterly releases), total net sales fell about 25% to roughly $13.0 billion, and the company posted a net loss near $985 million. Johnson was fired in April 2013 and successor Myron Ullman reinstated coupons and promotions, partially reversing the strategy.

source_backed_metrics.fiscal_2012_total_net_sales_usd: approximately 12.98 billion (down ~25% from ~$17.3 billion prior year)

owner_decision_context: CEO Ron Johnson, fresh from Apple, judged that JCP's coupon-and-sale model was inefficient and that customers would prefer simple, honest everyday prices. He committed to an abrupt, company-wide pricing transformation rather than testing it.
action_taken: Removed coupons and high-low discount/promotional pricing across all stores ('Fair and Square' everyday pricing), eliminating the discount signals core shoppers relied on; later partially reversed when coupons and sales were reinstated under the successor CEO.
outcome_evidence: Sequential double-digit comparable-store sales declines through 2012, ~25% drop in total net sales to ~$13.0 billion, and a ~$985 million net loss. Johnson was removed in April 2013 and the promotional model was reinstated, confirming the pricing action directly worsened the business.
source_limitations: WebFetch of sec.gov returned HTTP 403; the 10-K and quarterly figures are confirmed verbatim across WebSearch snippets attributed to JCP's SEC filings (8-K earnings releases, 10-K CIK 0001166126) and named journalism (TIME, Retail Dive). Q4 comp figure varies slightly by source (~-1.8% to -4.4% depending on adjustment) and is reported with that caveat.
directly_stated: 'Fair and Square' pricing announced Jan 25, 2012, effective Feb 1, 2012, eliminated coupons and promotional sales
Fiscal 2012 net sales fell about 25% to roughly $13.0 billion
Fiscal 2012 net loss was about $985 million ($4.49 per share)
Quarterly comparable-store sales declined 18.9%, 21.7%, and 26.1% in Q1-Q3 2012
Ron Johnson was removed in April 2013 and promotions/coupons were reinstated
inferred: The pricing overhaul, not exogenous demand, drove the collapse because the declines began immediately upon implementation and partially reversed after reinstatement
Core customer value perception was tied to discount signals (pricing-power misjudgment)
why_useful_for_opsiq: Textbook outcome-10 case: a deliberate strategic pricing action that worsened results, later reversed. Tests whether the engine recognizes that the owner's own decision (not market shock) was the proximate cause, and routes to re-evaluation of pricing power and customer value perception.
